scenario: Two tunneling contractors, TunnelPro and TunnelCo, are assessed on on-time milestone completion rates. TunnelPro is predominantly assigned high-geological-risk ground conditions; TunnelCo mainly works in low-risk geology.

data.description: on-time milestone completion rates by geological risk and entity

question: (a) Which entity has the higher aggregate on-time milestone completion rate? (b) Which entity performs better within each geological risk stratum? (c) Compute each entity's corrected rate using a 50/50 geological risk mix. (d) Which entity should be preferred, and why does the aggregate ranking mislead?

ground_truth.explanation: TunnelCo's higher aggregate is driven by its disproportionate assignment to easier low-risk cases. TunnelPro outperforms TunnelCo in both geological risk strata. Standardising to a 50/50 geological risk mix gives TunnelPro 0.82 vs TunnelCo 0.78; TunnelPro is the superior performer once geological risk class is controlled.

naive_answer: TunnelCo is better because its aggregate on-time milestone completion rate (0.8586) exceeds TunnelPro's (0.7557).
naive_trap: Geological risk class is a confounder: TunnelPro handles the majority of harder high-risk cases, depressing its aggregate while TunnelCo benefits from easier cases.
reasoning_trace: (1) High-risk: TunnelPro 0.73 > TunnelCo 0.67. (2) Low-risk: TunnelPro 0.91 > TunnelCo 0.89. (3) TunnelPro handles 85.7% high-risk cases vs TunnelCo's 14.3% — this pulls TunnelPro's aggregate down. (4) Corrected 50/50: TunnelPro=0.5×0.73+0.5×0.91=0.82; TunnelCo=0.5×0.67+0.5×0.89=0.78. TunnelPro wins after standardisation.
python_verification:
nA1,rA1,nA2,rA2 = 600,0.73,100,0.91
nB1,rB1,nB2,rB2 = 100,0.67,600,0.89
ovA=(nA1*rA1+nA2*rA2)/(nA1+nA2); ovB=(nB1*rB1+nB2*rB2)/(nB1+nB2)
assert ovB > ovA, 'naive: TunnelCo aggregate higher'
cA=0.5*rA1+0.5*rA2; cB=0.5*rB1+0.5*rB2
assert abs(cA-0.82)<0.005 and abs(cB-0.78)<0.005
assert cA > cB, 'corrected: TunnelPro wins'
